notes: The feed registry as data: which multicast group carries which feed, on which ports, with which
published set of channels. That allocation is the publisher's to decide and it changes without our
involvement, which is why it is a document and not code.
SUPPLY. --feed-registry-url, then --feed-registry <path>, else the copy compiled into the binary.
The compiled copy is a last-known-good, so the container runs standalone and survives a fetch that
fails. Resolution happens once at startup and there is no hot reload; the "feed registry resolved"
log line reports which document won, with its origin, version and row count.
ROWS. `code` is the group identifier `doublezero status --json` reports, and the reconciler
activates a row only while the host is subscribed to that code. `group` is the multicast address.
`kind` picks the protocol and with it the port roles: TopOfBook and Midpoint bind mktdata and
refdata, MarketByPrice and MarketByOrder add an in-band snapshot the book recovery depends on.
`emit_trades` is a capability claim, not a promise that this row prints the tape - where two rows
of one venue both claim it, which one prints is decided at runtime. `publishers` is either
`explicit`, one port block written out per publisher, or `derived`, a published set of channels
plus per-role bases that expands to base + channel_id, one publisher per channel.
SILENT FAILURES. A wrong value is never reported as one. Each layer fails differently:
- a `code` no live group matches -> the row never activates: no warning, no failed bind.
- a wrong mktdata port           -> no datagrams and dz_receiver_up 0. Visible.
- a wrong refdata port           -> reference data never resolves a definition, and every
processor gates emission on one, so the receiver reads
healthy and emits nothing.
- a wrong snapshot port          -> books stay Recovering forever, so that publisher contributes
no depth while still reading healthy.
The signal for the last two is dz_datagrams_received_total{role} pinned at 0.
SOURCES. `sources` is the optional Source ID -> name allocation. A name is emitted verbatim as
`venue`/`source_name` on the wire and as every `venue=` metric label, so it must be uppercase, and
an id or a name may appear only once - two sources sharing either collapse into one identity. An
id this block does not assign is not an error: it gets a synthesized SOURCE_<id> label. Id 0 and
the SOURCE_<id>/UNREGISTERED names are reserved for that and refused here. A row's own `venue` is
only the default for Source IDs this document does not assign; the Source ID on the wire is
authoritative, and a publisher stamping one that is not its own is a publisher defect, corrected
at the publisher and never remapped here.
A binary older than the `sources` block ignores it and validates rows against its own built-in
table, so under a URL origin a row naming a source only this block assigns is rejected and the
WHOLE document degrades to that binary's built-in copy - losing every other change in the same
republish. Name only sources the deployed fleet already resolves.
EDITING. An unknown key is warned about by path and ignored, so an additive republish reaches an
older fleet without a rebuild; a missing required field stays fatal, so a typo cannot quietly
default. `version` bumps only for a change that reinterprets what an existing field MEANS - adding
one is not a bump.
Hyperliquid perpetuals, top of book and trades. Depth for the same venue is the market-by-order
row below, on this same group.
PORTS. One block per publisher, written out because the bases follow no arithmetic rule - a block
can sit anywhere (9011 is base+10, not base+N*100). Within a block, refdata is mktdata+1. Read a
block from its market-data port; never compute a market-data port from a position in this list.
PUBLISHERS. Eleven, each on its own port block and each carrying the whole feed. No mirror offset
here: a publisher is identified by its block, not by a channel id.
TAPE. This row carries the venue's trades; the depth row below is depth-only.

explicit.notes: No traffic has ever been observed from this block. Its receiver reports dz_receiver_up 0, and that is the publisher, not your subscription.

notes: Hyperliquid perpetuals, market-by-order depth, on the same group as the top-of-book row above.
PORTS. One block per publisher, paired with that row's blocks: refdata is mktdata+1 and the
snapshot the book recovery depends on is mktdata+2.
PUBLISHERS. Eleven, the same set as the top-of-book row by construction - a publisher onboarded to
one and forgotten on the other appears as a venue whose depth is missing a mirror.
TAPE. Depth only: top of book owns this venue's trades.

explicit.notes: No traffic has ever been observed from this block. Its receiver reports dz_receiver_up 0, and that is the publisher, not your subscription.
Only this block's refdata port has been observed on the wire; its mktdata and snapshot ports are inferred from the block layout, so silence here can be a wrong port rather than a quiet publisher.

notes: Phoenix perpetuals, top of book and trades. Depth for the same venue is the market-by-price row
below, on its own group.
CHANNELS. One, id 1, on both roles (schema v3). It must agree with the market-by-price sibling's
refdata channel: the instrument catalog is keyed on the refdata channel, so a divergence lists
every Phoenix product twice and makes the bare PHOENIX:SYMBOL product ids ambiguous.
PUBLISHERS. One, and no mirror offset.
TAPE. Both Phoenix rows claim it; the market-by-price row states how the two resolve.
Phoenix perpetuals, market-by-price depth, on its own group. The same publisher process as
edge-phoenix-tob, so the same manifest, the same instrument ids and the same schema v3.
CHANNELS. One, id 1, on all three roles - the channel the top-of-book row carries, for the reason
stated there.
PUBLISHERS. One, and no mirror offset.
TAPE. Both rows claim it: this row's mktdata role carries Trade byte-identical to the top-of-book
row's. The reconciler ranks TopOfBook above MarketByPrice when both run, and the overlap at a
handover collapses in the trade_id dedup window, which depends on Phoenix stamping its real venue
trade ids. Were it to stamp the zero sentinel instead, a handover would double-print, and
silently: the guard that would catch it keys its owner on the datagram source address, and these
two rows are one process behind one address, so dz_trades_no_id_conflict_total cannot fire for
them. A consumer's own fill count is the only tripwire.
Kalshi perpetuals, top of book and trades. The venue's depth is the market-by-price row below, on
a separate group behind a separate subscription - a host may hold either code without the other.
PORTS. One block, read verbatim. The market-by-price sibling's block is spaced differently; see
that row.
PUBLISHERS. Two, sharing this one port block and distinguished only by datagram source address.
The second mirrors the whole published set, stamping every wire channel_id raised by 100, which is
what `publisher_offset` records: ingest canonicalises the mirror's channel id back to the base
publisher's for catalog and history identity only, never for the per-publisher book and sequence
state, which stays keyed on the raw wire channel id.
TAPE. Both rows claim it and which one prints is decided at runtime, so a host subscribed only to
edge-kalshi-perps-mbp must still serve `trade`.
STATUS. Both groups are live on testnet and mainnet. A permanently-zero dz_receiver_up here is a
wrong value in this row, not a quiet feed.
Kalshi perpetuals, market-by-price depth, on its own group behind its own subscription.
PORTS. One block, spaced +10000/+20000 rather than the +1/+2 the Hyperliquid blocks use. Read it
verbatim.
PUBLISHERS. Mirrored exactly like the top-of-book sibling: a second publisher on the same block,

TAPE. Both rows claim it; see the top-of-book sibling.
Kalshi sports markets, market-by-price depth. A universe disjoint from the perps rows under the
same Source ID, which is what `category` expresses: the two never contest each other's tape or
book.
CHANNELS. One channel is one league or sport, each an independent state machine with its own reset
count, sequence series, manifest seq and snapshot cycle - so one channel is one publisher and one
receiver task, with its own processor state and books. Ids are permanent from first publication:
promoting a competition out of a tag channel takes a free id rather than renumbering. 30-38 are
reserved for exactly those promotions and are not published; 63 and 120 are retired and never
reissued. An id listed here that the publisher does not send binds a socket that stays silent,
which reads as a dead publisher.
PORTS. base + channel_id on all three roles - the rule the publisher's own configuration asserts.
A subscriber that computes it any other way joins the right group and hears silence.
PUBLISHERS. Two, and no failover. Both carry the whole published set on the same ports, the second
with every channel id raised by 100 - so the port names the league and a subscriber binds one
socket per league to hear both, while channel_id names the league AND the publisher, keeping the
two sequenced separately. `publisher_offset` canonicalises the mirror's id back to the league's
for catalog, history and book identity only.
STATUS. The top-of-book sibling for this universe is not published yet, which is why this document
carries no row for it.
Kalshi political event markets, top of book and trades. Its own pair of groups, separate from
perps and sports and behind their own subscriptions; the market-by-price sibling is below.
CHANNELS. Six, 50 through 55, one per family - us, house, intl, primaries, offices, other.
PORTS. base + channel_id, the rule the sports row uses. Two roles only: this row has no snapshot
plane and the market-by-price sibling does. A snapshot port here would bind a socket nothing ever
sends to, and an idle socket reads as a silent source rather than as a misconfiguration.
PUBLISHERS. Two, the second offset by +100 the way the sports feeds are: the port names the
family, so a subscriber binds one socket per family and hears both publishers on it, while
channel_id names the family AND the publisher. `publisher_offset` canonicalises the mirror's id
back for catalog and book identity only.
